title: Chabuca Granda's birth chart
metaDescription: Chabuca Granda's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 10.9° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Five of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Virgo — the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter and Saturn. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Virgo, but precisely: 10.9°, second decan, 10°–20°, under Saturn in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 5.7° Virgo, Venus at 27.8° Virgo, Mars at 29.3° Scorpio. Mercury in an earth sign reads as a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; Venus in an earth sign reads as taste for the substantial and the lasting; Mars in a water sign reads as drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Venus and Mars — a sextile holding at 1.5°. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift. Behind it, Jupiter opposition Uranus at 1.8°, and the Sun sextile Pluto at 2.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Uranus while both square Mars. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. Neptune stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, five sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Moon in Taurus at 13.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Virgo at 5.7° is in exaltation; Venus in Virgo at 27.8° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Scorpio at 29.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Virgo at 1.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 6 earth, 3 water, 1 fire by element and 6 mutable, 3 fixed, 1 cardinal by mode. An earth emphasis reads as trust in the tangible: the plan matters less than whether the thing stands up. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Uranus was retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.7° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 13.9°.
